{"metadata":{"description":"PR Genius — 提交前改进顾问 + 大型开源项目 PR 知识库","id":"gh:1287261026","install_available":true,"language":"Python","name":"pr-genius","slug":"zsxh1990/pr-genius","topics":["ai-agents","cli","code-review","coding-agent","dsh","dsh-plugin","github","mcp","open-source","pr-review","python"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"PR Genius — 提交前改进顾问 + 大型开源项目 PR 知识库"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"type: Knowledge Bundle
title: PR Genius — the board for the PRs you sent out
description: Project ma"},{"id":"p2s2","text":"nagement for your outbound open-source contributions — not a code reviewer. Know which of your open "},{"id":"p2s3","text":"PRs needs you today, and what to do about it.
version: 2.2.3
created: 2026-07-01
updated: 2026-10-17"},{"id":"p2s4","text":"
author: zsxh1990
conforms_to: OKF v0.1 (Sudhakaran88/okf-conformance) + agent_guidelines extension"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"mcp-name: io.github.zsxh1990/pr-genius"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"# PR Genius"},{"id":"p5s1","text":"> Somewhere in your GitHub there are PRs you have stopped opening.
>
> One needs a rebase you keep m"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"eaning to do. One has been red for four days and
> nobody told you. Three have sat untouched for thr"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"ee weeks. And one you avoid
> entirely, because opening it would mean confirming that it is dead."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"**PR Genius is the board for that work** — the contributions you sent out into
other people's reposi"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"tories, where you have no tracker, no standup, and no
clue."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"It is **not** a code reviewer. By default it never reads your diff, and it will
never tell you your "},{"id":"p7s2","text":"code is correct. There are good tools for that, and this is
not one of them."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"**Unlike PR-Agent or CodeRabbit, this tool does not read your diff.** It does
not write review comme"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"nts on your code, and it is not an LLM. It scores a PR
against **61 anti-patterns** harvested from P"},{"id":"p8s3","text":"Rs that actually got rejected, and
answers a different question from the one a review bot answers."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"It answers the question a working contributor actually has on a Tuesday
morning: **of everything I h"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"ave sent out, what do I touch today — and what
exactly do I do about it?**"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"## Why this exists"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"GitHub remembers the PR."},{"id":"p12s1","text":"It does **not** remember why you closed your third attempt on a given repo.
What worked. What didn't"},{"id":"p12s2","text":". Which reviewer actually answers and which commented
once and vanished. Whether the thing that got "},{"id":"p12s3","text":"you bounced last time was the
size, the missing issue link, or the tone."},{"id":"p13s1","text":"That knowledge lives in your head. It dies when the session ends."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"PR Genius is where it goes instead."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"> A Repo Profile captures the **what** a project wants.
> A case study captures the **how** a contri"},{"id":"p15s2","text":"bution landed or died.
> Your own status history captures the **then-what** — how long it waited, wh"},{"id":"p15s3","text":"at
> changed, whether it ever came back."},{"id":"p16s1","text":"Neither a code reviewer nor a chat model can have the third one. They see your
PR once, in someone e"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"lse's repo. This sees your portfolio over months."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"## What it knows"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"| It knows | Why it matters to you |"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"| **How 67 large projects actually behave** — merge rates, review cadence, what gets closed | You st"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"op guessing what `encode/httpx` wants and start matching it |
| **Why real PRs got rejected** — writ"},{"id":"p19s3","text":"ten down, with the evidence | You stop repeating the mistake that already cost someone else three we"},{"id":"p19s4","text":"eks |
| **What your own PRs did over time** — which state each sat in, for how long | You find out a"},{"id":"p19s5","text":" PR died *while it was dying*, not three weeks later |
| **The policy of the repo you are aiming at*"},{"id":"p19s6","text":"* | A `Fixes #N` in the body is still the single most common reason a first PR gets bounced |"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"Numbers, for the sceptical: 753 loaded patterns, 190 harvested failed-PR
observations, 68 repo profi"},{"id":"p20s2","text":"les, 302 reviewed cases. Those are receipts for the
sentence above, not the point of it — every one "},{"id":"p20s3","text":"of them is verified against the
live tree on each release by `scripts/verify_claims.py`."},{"id":"p21s1","text":"One of those corpora deserves a caveat: `success-patterns/` is
**retrieval/reference only** and is *"},{"id":"p21s2","text":"*not wired into scoring**. It is browsable
context, not a positive-feedback system, and no verdict h"},{"id":"p21s3","text":"as ever been changed
by it. The 61 anti-patterns are what actually move the risk tier."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"## The nine states are nine decisions"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"A number on a dashboard tells you something is wrong. A *state* tells you what
to do about it."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"| State | What it means for you today |"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"| `NEEDS_REBASE` | Twenty minutes of work and this PR is still alive. |
| `CI_FAILING` | It has been"},{"id":"p25s2","text":" red for days and nobody was going to tell you. |
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p26s1","text":"## What it will never do"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"Stated plainly, because the rest of this page is worthless if these are fuzzy:"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"- **It will not tell you your code is correct.** It does not judge your logic.
You can hand it a dif"},{"id":"p28s2","text":"f (`--diff`) and it will flag install commands, downloads
piped into a shell, and secret-shaped stri"},{"id":"p28s3","text":"ngs — a keyword pass, not a review.
Without one, it looks at the summary counts only.
- **It will no"},{"id":"p28s4","text":"t write or send anything on your behalf** unless you pass an
explicit `--confirm`. Every mutating co"},{"id":"p28s5","text":"mmand is dry-run by default.
- **It will not phone home.** Analysis is local: no LLM, no API key, no"},{"id":"p28s6","text":" network
call. The commands that touch GitHub do it with *your* token and only for PR
metadata. Ther"},{"id":"p28s7","text":"e is no telemetry — see docs/ADOPTION_DATA.md
for what is measured instead and why we chose not to b"},{"id":"p28s8","text":"uild the rest.
- **It will not pretend.** If a fact is not verified, the docs say so. This
page has "},{"id":"p28s9","text":"been wrong before and the corrections are in the
changelog."},{"id":"p29s1","text":"## What this tool is NOT"},{"id":"p30s1","text":"The section above is about behaviour. This one is about **roles** — the jobs
people assume it does b"},{"id":"p30s2","text":"ecause of what it looks like. It does not do them, and
that is a boundary, not an oversight."},{"id":"p31s1","text":"| It is not | What that means in practice |"},{"id":"p32s1","text":"| **A merge gate** | It never blocks a merge and never fails a job. The GitHub Action offers `commen"},{"id":"p32s2","text":"t_mode` and `apply_labels` only — there is no required-check integration, because a "gate" that can "},{"id":"p32s3","text":"be ignored is worse than no gate. If you want it to block, wire the Action's exit into *your* branch"},{"id":"p32s4","text":" protection yourself. |
| **A PR title linter** | It will not fail a PR for a malformed title. It wi"},{"id":"p32s5","text":"ll tell you that a missing `Fixes #N` is the most common reason a first PR gets bounced, and leave t"},{"id":"p32s6","text":"he decision to you. |
| **A CODEOWNERS-aware reviewer** | It does not know who owns which file, and "},{"id":"p32s7","text":"will not route or request reviewers. |
| **A code reviewer** | See above. It never reads your diff u"},{"id":"p32s8","text":"nless you hand one to `--diff`, and what it does then is a keyword pass. |
| **A positive-feedback s"},{"id":"p32s9","text":"ystem** | `success-patterns/` (692 of the 753 loaded patterns) is **retrieval/reference only** and i"},{"id":"p32s10","text":"s **not wired into scoring**. Only the 61 anti-patterns can move a verdict. |"},{"id":"p33s1","text":"The last row is the one worth internalising: the corpus is large, but the part
that *scores* is smal"},{"id":"p33s2","text":"l on purpose — it is the part backed by PRs that actually
got rejected."}],"truncated":true}
